quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Clap the two syllables: WIN-dow. At the start of the first syllable, are your lips rounded, or is your lip touching your teeth?
quests.explanation: 'Window' starts with /w/ at the front of a stressed syllable, where consonants are at their clearest. The lips round and spring open; touching the lip to the teeth gives 'vindow'. A longer word doesn't change how the first sound is made. It only tempts you to rush it.
quests.mouthPosition: Round your lips tightly, spring them open into 'win', and keep your teeth off your lip.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The stress falls on the first syllable. Say it with extra push: is there a puff of air right at the start?
quests.explanation: 'Coffee' begins with a stressed /k/: the back of the tongue releases with a clear puff. Voicing it gives 'goffee'. After the /k/ comes a lip-teeth hiss, so keep the /k/ firm before you hurry on.
quests.mouthPosition: Lift the back of your tongue to the soft palate and release with a strong puff into 'off', then finish with a quick 'ee'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Before you say the rest of the word, check your tongue: is it pulled back and untouched, or pressing the ridge?
quests.explanation: 'Rabbit' begins with /r/: the tongue pulls back without touching the roof. Touching the ridge gives /l/ and 'labbit'. The /b/ in the middle needs a full lip closure, so the whole word has to stay clear.
quests.mouthPosition: Draw the tongue back and up with its sides near the upper back teeth, tip free, then glide into 'rab'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Between the two vowels, does the voice keep running? Say it and feel for a steady hum.
quests.explanation: 'Lazy' has /z/ between the stressed 'la' and the weak 'ee', and the buzz carries on between the vowels. Using /s/ gives 'lacy', a different word. Voiced consonants in the middle of a word need their buzz.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'lay-', put the tongue tip near the ridge and let a buzz run through before the weak 'ee'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The middle consonant begins the weak second syllable. Is it a clean, voiceless stop?
quests.explanation: 'Ticket' has /k/ in the middle, at the start of an unstressed syllable. Weak syllables tend to be short and the consonant can go soft. Voicing gives 'tigget'. Keep the /k/ crisp even though the vowel after it is weak.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'ti-', lift the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice, release quickly into the weak 'it', and finish with 't'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The middle nasal is followed by a hard G. Which part of your tongue is raised for the nasal?
quests.explanation: 'Finger' has /ŋ/ in the middle, followed by a sounded /g/. Unlike 'singer', the G is pronounced here. The nasal is made at the back of the tongue; using /n/ gives 'fin-ger', with the tongue in the wrong place for the /g/.
quests.mouthPosition: The back of the tongue goes up and hums, then lets go into a voiced 'g' before the weak 'er'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The last syllable is weak. Do your lips close at the end, or does the tongue tip lift?
quests.explanation: 'Open' ends in a weak syllable with /n/: the tongue tip on the ridge and voiced air through the nose. Closing the lips gives /m/ and 'opem'. The vowel in the last syllable is tiny, and the consonant shouldn't vanish with it.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'oh-p', lift your tongue tip to the ridge and hum through your nose, with your lips staying open.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word ends with a very short syllable. Does the tongue tip finish on the ridge with air around the sides?
quests.explanation: 'Travel' ends in a weak syllable with /l/: the tongue tip presses the ridge and air flows around the sides. Skipping it leaves 'trave', and swapping in /n/ gives 'travven'. The /l/ can carry the syllable on its own.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'trav-', press your tongue tip on the ridge behind your upper teeth and let voiced air run around the sides.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The last syllable is tiny. Hold its consonant: are your lips pressed together while it hums?
quests.explanation: 'Problem' ends with /m/ in a weak syllable: the lips close and the voice flows through the nose. Using /n/ gives 'problen'. Closing the lips is easy to forget when the vowel before it is tiny.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'prob-l', close both lips and hum through your nose as the weak syllable ends.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word starts with a glide. Does your tongue seal against the roof, or just rise toward it?
quests.explanation: 'Yesterday' begins with /j/: the tongue glides up toward the palate with no closure. Sealing gives /dʒ/ and 'jesterday'. In a three-syllable word it's easy to over-articulate the first consonant, so keep it smooth.
quests.mouthPosition: Raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof as if for 'ee', glide into 'yes', and carry on through the rhythm of 'ter-day'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Stress falls on the middle syllable. Does the consonant that opens it come with a puff?
quests.explanation: 'Potato' has /t/ at the start of the stressed middle syllable, so it gets a clear puff. Voicing it gives 'podato'. The second /t/ is lighter in fast speech, but this first one stays crisp.
quests.mouthPosition: After the weak 'puh', tap your tongue tip firmly on the ridge and release with a puff into the stressed 'tay'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: After the stressed first syllable, do your lips close for the middle consonant?
quests.explanation: 'Family' has /m/ after the stressed 'fa': the lips close and voiced air goes through the nose. Using /n/ gives 'fanily'. Because the middle vowel is weak, the /m/ can get lost, so close the lips.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'fa-', close both lips and hum through your nose, then open into the quick 'uh-lee'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The middle consonant follows the stressed first syllable. Is it voiced or voiceless?
quests.explanation: 'Chocolate' has /k/ in the middle: voiceless, straight after the stressed first syllable. Voicing it gives 'choggolate'. The word is often said with two or three syllables, but the /k/ stays a clear closure either way.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'chock-', lift the back of your tongue with no voice, release quickly, and let the weak ending fade into 'lit'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The middle of the word is spelled G. Is the sound voiced or voiceless?
quests.explanation: 'Vegetable' has /dʒ/ in the middle, spelled G, and it's voiced. Using /tʃ/ gives 'vetchtable'. Many speakers say it as three syllables, 'VEJ-tuh-bul', and the /dʒ/ stays clear.
quests.mouthPosition: Once the short 've-' is said, seal your tongue against the roof behind the ridge with voice on, and release into a buzzy hush before 'tuh-bul'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The middle consonant follows a hiss. Is the lip closure voiced or voiceless?
quests.explanation: 'Hospital' has /p/ after /s/: the lips close with no voice and a tiny puff. Voicing gives 'hosbital'. After the hiss the /p/ is short and quiet, so it's easy to swallow, but it's needed.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'hos-', close your lips with no voice for a quick 'p', and release into the weak 'ih-tul'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: In the middle of the word, is the lip-teeth sound buzzing?
quests.explanation: 'Television' has /v/ in the middle, and it's voiced. Using /f/ gives 'telefission'. The word also contains /ʒ/, but the question is about the lip-teeth consonant.
quests.mouthPosition: In the middle of the word, bring lip and upper teeth together with a buzz, brief but audible, before the final 'zhun'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The middle sound is spelled CI. Is it thin and high, or broad and soft?
quests.explanation: 'Official' has /ʃ/ in the middle, spelled CI. The tongue pulls back and the lips round for a broad hush. A thin /s/ gives 'offisial'. In longer words, CI, TI and SI often stand for /ʃ/.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'uh-fi', pull your tongue slightly back, round your lips, and hush air through before the weak 'ul'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The middle consonant sits just after a stop and before a vowel. Does air keep flowing past your teeth?
quests.explanation: 'Together' has /ð/ after the stressed 'ge': the tongue tip touches the back of the teeth and voiced air flows. Using /d/ gives 'togedder'. The /g/ earlier in the word is a separate sound.
quests.mouthPosition: Mid-word, your tongue tip rests lightly on the back of your upper teeth while the voice runs; no tap, no seal.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: After the short 'i', does the tongue tip press the ridge or stay back?
quests.explanation: 'Pillow' has /l/ in the middle: the tongue tip presses the ridge and releases into 'ow'. Pulling the tongue back gives /r/ and 'pirrow'. The doubled L in the spelling is one sound.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'pi-', press your tongue tip on the ridge behind your upper teeth, voice on, and drop into the weak 'oh'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: After the vowel, which part of the tongue is raised for the nasal: tip or back?
quests.explanation: 'Hungry' has /ŋ/ followed by /g/ and /r/. The nasal is made at the back of the tongue. Using /n/ gives 'hun-gry', which sounds odd because the G is sounded here.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'hu-', raise the back of your tongue and hum through your nose, then release into 'g' and 'r'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word has two nasals made at the lips. Focus on the one in the middle: do your lips close?
quests.explanation: 'Memory' has /m/ at the start and another /m/ in the middle: the lips close for both. The middle one begins a weak syllable, so it can blur into /n/ ('menory'). Close the lips.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'mem-', close your lips again and hum through your nose, then glide into the weak 'ree'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: After the nasal, which lip-teeth sound follows? Is it voiced?
quests.explanation: 'Comfortable' has /f/ after /m/: the lips open, the top teeth touch the bottom lip, and voiceless air hisses through. Voicing gives 'comvortable'. Many speakers shorten the word to 'COMF-ter-bul', but the /f/ stays clear.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'kum-', open your lips, rest your top teeth on your bottom lip, and hiss with no voice before 'ter-bul'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Between the stressed first syllable and the next, is the sound broad and soft, or thin and high?
quests.explanation: 'Dictionary' has /ʃ/ in the middle, spelled TI. The tongue pulls back and the lips round for a hush. A thin /s/ gives 'diksionary'. The stress sits on the first syllable, so the rest can blur, but the /ʃ/ should stay distinct.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'dik-', pull your tongue slightly back and round your lips for a quick hush, then finish with 'uh-neh-ree'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Two hissing sounds sit in the middle of this word. Do both stay voiceless?
quests.explanation: 'Necessary' has /s/ twice in the middle, spelled C and SS. Both are voiceless. Voicing gives 'nezessary'. Keep the tongue tip forward and don't let a buzz creep in.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'nes-', hiss with your tongue tip near the ridge and no voice, then glide through 'uh-seh-ree'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word ends with a hiss too, so focus on the consonant in the middle. Broad or thin?
quests.explanation: 'Delicious' has /ʃ/ in the middle, spelled CI, before the final /s/. Using /s/ in the middle gives 'delisious'. The /ʃ/ starts the last syllable, so hold it for a moment.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'dih-li', pull your tongue back, round your lips, and hush air out before the weak 'us'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The first consonant after the weak first syllable: is it voiced or voiceless?
quests.explanation: 'December' has /s/ at the start of the stressed syllable, even though the letter is C. Voicing gives 'dezember'. After the weak first syllable, the hiss opens the stressed one.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'dih-', put your tongue tip near the ridge and hiss with no voice before 'sem-ber'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: At the very end of this long word, is the last sound voiced?
quests.explanation: 'Restaurant' ends in /nt/: the tongue tip closes for a voiceless /t/ after the nasal. Many speakers drop it and say 'restauran', but keeping it makes the word clearer. Voicing gives 'restaurand'.
quests.mouthPosition: Following the weak 'ruh-n', keep your tongue tip on the ridge and stop the air with a silent 't'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: After the nasal, the last sound matches the nasal's voice. Does it buzz?
quests.explanation: 'Understand' ends in /nd/, both voiced, after the stressed 'stan'. The final /d/ is often dropped in fast speech. Keep the buzz to the end: devoicing gives 'understant'.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'stan', hum with the tongue tip on the ridge and close the air off with your voice still on for a voiced 'd'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word begins with a lip sound. Is there a buzz before the lips open?
quests.explanation: 'Beautiful' begins with /b/ before the /j/ glide of 'byoo'. Devoicing gives 'peautiful'. The lips close with voice on, then release into the glide.
quests.mouthPosition: Close your lips with voice on, release softly into 'byoo', and finish with the weak 'ti-ful'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The GH makes the middle of this word look odd. Say it slowly: what happens at your lips right after the long 'ay'?
quests.explanation: 'Neighbor' has /b/ in the middle: a full lip closure. Using /v/ gives 'neivor'. The silent GH makes the middle of the word look unfamiliar, so trust the sound.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'nay-', close both lips fully with voice on and release gently into the weak 'er'.
